prompts.display_text: Pin Preston, England, where the first British converts were baptized in 1837.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on Preston, Lancashire, where the first missionaries to Britain preached and baptized their first converts in 1837.
prompts.citation: Church newsroom UK, History of the Church in the British Isles; Ensign Sept. 1971, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Heber C. Kimball and other missionaries first preached in Preston's Vauxhall Chapel in July 1837. On July 30, only 10 days after they arrived, Kimball baptized the first converts in England in the River Ribble as thousands watched. The Preston Ward, founded in 1837, is the Church's oldest continuing congregation.

prompts.display_text: Pin a non-US country where the Church President himself dedicated a temple before 1990.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the United States with a temple dedicated before 1990 by the sitting President of the Church.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated-by column) and Wikipedia temple articles, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Before 1990 only a handful of temples outside the United States were dedicated by the sitting Church President: Heber J. Grant at Cardston, David O. McKay at Bern, Hamilton and London, Spencer W. Kimball at São Paulo and Tokyo, and Ezra Taft Benson at Frankfurt. Most of the 1983 to 1986 temples abroad were dedicated by Gordon B. Hinckley while he served as a counselor in the First Presidency.

prompts.display_text: Pin a place where Latter-day Saint servicemen held some of the first Church meetings.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory where Latter-day Saints serving in the U.S. military held some of the earliest Church meetings or groups (1940s-1950s).
prompts.citation: Church History Department, Global Histories country chronologies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: During and after World War II, Latter-day Saints in the U.S. military met wherever they were stationed. In many places these servicemen's groups were the first Church meetings held, and some invited local friends who later joined the Church.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: 1945-47: first Church meetings in Korea held by Latter-day Saints in the U.S. military, who invited Korean friends.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: 1953: Luzon Servicemen's District organized; 1957: Navy serviceman Kendall B. Schaefermeyer baptized four Filipinos.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: 1956: American military personnel and families held the first Latter-day Saint group meetings in Spain.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: 1944-46: first Church members on Guam were with the U.S. military.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: 1944-45: groups of Latter-day Saint servicemen were organized throughout Italy.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: July 1944: first members of the Church in Costa Rica were U.S. servicemen.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: April 29, 1945: servicemen at Keflavik organized a Church group; servicemen's branch in 1947.

answers.name: Marshall Islands
answers.fact: 1940s: first Church services held by American military personnel during World War II.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: 1940s: small groups of servicemen held Church meetings in members' homes.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: 1950s: earliest known Latter-day Saints in Portugal were U.S. servicemen at Lajes Field, Azores.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: 1956: Chin Mu-tsung met the Church through Latter-day Saint servicemen and was baptized.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the Bible records a person building, using or seeing an altar, Noah's and Moses's altars and Jerusalem aside.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where the Bible records a person building, using or seeing an altar, Noah's and Moses's altars and Jerusalem aside
prompts.citation: Genesis 12:7; 26:25; 35:7; Numbers 23:1-29; Joshua 8:30; 22:10; Judges 13:20; 1 Samuel 7:17; 1 Kings 18:30; 2 Kings 16:10; Acts 17:23
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Altars mark where people met God. Abraham built them at Shechem and Bethel and Joshua on Mount Ebal, all in the West Bank, while Elijah's showdown altar stood on Carmel in Israel (1 Kings 18:30). Balaam's seven altars rose in Moab, Paul found an altar to the unknown god in Athens, and Ahaz copied an altar he admired in Damascus (2 Kings 16:10).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord on Carmel, Isaac built one at Beersheba, and Manoah offered at Zorah (1 Kings 18:30; Genesis 26:25; Judges 13:20).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Abraham built altars at Shechem and Bethel, Joshua on Mount Ebal, Samuel at Ramah, and the eastern tribes raised the great altar Ed in the land of Canaan by the Jordan (Genesis 12:7; 35:7; Joshua 8:30; 22:10-11; 1 Samuel 7:17).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul found an altar in Athens inscribed to the unknown god (Acts 17:23).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Balaam had seven altars built on the heights of Moab (Numbers 23:1).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: King Ahaz saw an altar at Damascus and sent its pattern home to copy (2 Kings 16:10).
